explanation: Backtrack from every board cell. A set of coordinate pairs records only the cells on the current path; remove each mark on return so another path can reuse that cell.
timeComplexity: O(R times C times 4^L) upper bound for R rows, C columns, and word length L. Every board cell can start a path with at most four choices per character; no branch exceeds the word length or available cell count.
spaceComplexity: O(min(L,RC)) auxiliary space: the used set and active recursion contain only the current path, bounded by both word length L and RC cells.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The current recursion path spells the matched word prefix and marks exactly its used cells. A next step is allowed only to an unmarked orthogonal matching cell, preserving the no-reuse rule. Trying every neighbor and every starting cell explores all valid paths; removing marks on return makes the search exhaustive without changing the board.
walkthrough: On board ["ab","cd"], start at a in the top-left, move right to b, then down to d. These three different orthogonally adjacent cells spell "abd", so return true.
edgeCases: A diagonal move is not allowed.
A cell cannot be reused in the same word path.
The board is restored after backtracking, even after a failed branch.
